# Vessantaracariya (Cp 9)
**ID:** Cp 9
**Section:** Cariyāpiṭaka (cp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vessantaracariya* ("The Conduct of Vessantara", Cp 9 or Cp I.9) is the ninth narrative of the *Cariyāpiṭaka* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [Bareau; Wood 2005; Matsumura 1980; SuttaCentral]. Rather than employing the standard narrative label *jātaka*, the collection frames its episodes as *cariya* ("conduct") to illustrate the Bodhisatta's perfection of specific virtues; the *Vessantaracariya* belongs to the opening set of ten narratives dedicated to the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) [Wood 2005]. Traditional poetic accounts associate King Vessantara's extreme generosity with the era of the past Buddha Kassapa [Jennings 1948], focusing on his readiness to renounce his children, wife, and wealth for the attainment of omniscience (*sabbaññuta*) [Bareau].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify thematic and passage-level discussions in the *Milindapañha*, namely the *Paṭhavicalanapañha* (Mil 5.1.4) and the *Vessantarapañha* (Mil 6.3.1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus demonstrates substantial text reuse across Pali literature, most heavily with the text's commentary, the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (65 matches), as well as the canonical *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547), the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Kururājacariya* (Cp 3), and the *Pakiṇṇaka-gantha-saṅgaho Vessantarāgīti* [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, the Vessantara cycle constitutes one of the most famous Buddhist narratives, paralleled by the *Viśvantara Jātaka* in Āryaśūra's Sanskrit *Jātakamālā* and the *Viśvantarāvadāna* (no. 23) in Kṣemendra's *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* [Wood 2005; Matsumura 1980]. Automatic cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus also match passages of the text with Tibetan translations of the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155), the *Jātakamālā* (D4150), and the *Śrīsena-avadāna* (D0349), as well as Sanskrit versions of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* and the *Lalitavistara* [DharmaNexus].
